txt: A strikingly handsome man looks straight at you, his head crowned with a wide-brim hat. His hair is dark as an oil slick and his jaw is the most perfectly chiselled thing you've ever seen.
Her shoulder bones crack as she shrugs. "Maybe. Probably not. Makes no difference to me either way."
No response. Wherever this woman is, your words fail to reach her.
Nothing. Her smile just keeps widening; her hair is grey like lead.
She cups her ear and leans forward. "Did you just call me a *lady*, xerife?"
She glares at you. "Oh, this *xerife* is a smart one."
She looks you over and scoffs. "You're right, lawman. *I'm* the one who should take *my* health more seriously. Thank you for looking out for me..."
She raises her boot, slowly -- with contempt -- and says. "I'm starting to think you should let me get back to Gabriel Buenguerro. You're no Gabriel..."
She shrugs. "Whatever stupid things they put in the lorry, I imagine."
She's wearing sturdy worker's boots made of black leather. Buckles run across. The sole is also made of leather.
The small wrinkled woman does not greet you. She nods along to something on her radio. A photograph is clutched in her hands and there is a warm smile on her face.
The woman is still hunched over the railing, her head swaying to the music, her eyes looking at nothing in particular.
The woman looks at nothing, her eyes closed and her lips moving.
The woman still has her eyes fixed on the photograph in her hands. In the background, the radio plays.
The woman sways her wrinkled shell back and forth, a strange grin across her face.
The woman's malevolent cackling fills the roundabout.
"'In the middle of this town there's a ghostly motorway -- it takes all the people where they want to stay'..."
"'They say I've been away on a kind of holiday'..." She replies, silently.
"*Ah*. And what do I care about the Union boss? He's not Gabriel, he's not Franconegro. He's not even Hermenegildo the Hand."
"*Hosiannna...*" A sigh escapes her lips, then silence, as she stares within herself.
"*O sim*..." The woman stares at you, her mind elsewhere now, on other matters.
"*Oh meu deus*, the Lawman solved the case..." She lights the cigarette. A white cloud of smoke disappears into her mouth.
"*Someone* was..." She nods as though her meaning were perfectly clear.
"*This* is Gabriel Buenguerro..." She shows you the photograph in the lavish amber frame.
"*Xerife*, what you understand wouldn't fill a pamphlet..."
"...seems like a bit of an idiot." She breathes out. The air tastes sweet.
"A pale dream, is what it is." She nods her head according to a rhythm known only to her -- staring at the photo in her hands.
"And dark. And the process begins. Erasure. Kilometre by kilometre. In any direction. The Motorway South is a road you cannot come back from."
"And here I was thinking you were an idiot." She breathes out and the air tastes sweet. "So, are you? An idiot, I mean."
"And that's just fine with me. I don't mind becoming vapour. I *like* vapour..." She gathers a cloud of smoke in her mouth, then slowly exhales.
"And what *is* that?" She sticks a filterless cigarette into a cigarette holder and reaches for the light.

"Back in Mesque during the time of the Revolution." The smile returns to her face. "The sidewalks and cafes are filled with young people... I was on my way to see a new boiadeiro picture starring Gabriel Buenguerro."
"Beautiful... it's beautiful."
"Because I'm one of the best camionneurs around, that's why. I drive routes no one else will."
"Because they can no longer recognize the person I once was."
"Diamonds are good for you, lawman. You should try them sometime. Make yourself pretty like Eva Deshoras."
"Diamonds."
"Did you just call me a *lady*, xerife?"

"Don't be stupid. The boiadeiro returns from the Western Plain a *changed* man. One night, as he and his beloved are out walking along the River Magritte, she pleads with him to give up his riding and settle down..."
"Easy. It's the skinny man who thinks he's a poet -- never trust a poet..." She squints across the square. "Also, he's the only one I can see from here."
"Good. I don't care about drugs. Little molecules. They're nothing." She glances wistfully at the photo.

"He was the biggest star of his day. Girls used to faint in the aisles of the cinema whenever he came on the screen, and school boys used to memorize all his lines..." She leans back, savouring the world she's conjured up.
"Heroic doses, *xerife*. Heroic."
"How should I know? Do I look like I spend a lot of time with the other camionneurs -- sniffing around -- when I have my movies to go to..."
"Huh?" That flicked a switch somewhere. "What is it? What do you want?"
"I quit concerning myself with that a long time ago." She smiles a careless smile. "Besides, I don't drive the lorry for the cargo, if you know what I mean..."

"I wasn't dreaming. I was *there*, lawman. It was early spring and 'The Man Behind The Black Sun' had just come out. The posters were twenty metres tall. Everything was golden..." Her eyes narrow and she appears to take your measure.
"I would never make fun of a real lawman, *xerife*."
"I'm a lady like you're Gabriel Buenguerro -- only in dreams."
"I'm not that either, *xerife*." Her smile dissipates. "I've gone too far from it all to remember what was between my legs. It doesn't work like that on the *long haul*."
"I'm only terrifying to small children. And to those who used to know me."
"I'm terrifying to small children. And to those who used to know me."
"I've only felt it in the distance. When I was a child..." She goes silent, her eyes close and her hands shake. "A child. Rowing on the lake."
"If you don't know, pfft!" She flicks her wrist in a gesture of casual dismissal.
"If you wait long enough, it's going to be much more than just 'love'... It's going to be the entire history -- vapourised."
"In the belly of an airship, behind steel windows -- so you don't look straight into it. It's not *advised* to look into it."
"Irmão..." she breathes out. "I already *am* dust."
"Is that all you wanted to know, lawman?"
"Is that all you woke me up to say?"
"It was," she shrugs. "And then it was no more. And I was no longer holding my father's hand. He was no longer descending the stairs in Raehl. The crowd had gone silent."

"It's a point you cannot come back from. Your mind becomes so radiant with the past -- there is a flip." She flicks the ash from her cigarette. "Instead of writing, it erases memory. Nearing some kind of..." She shakes her head. "Indescribable *finale*."
"It's a story us longhaulsmen tell -- longhaulsmen, *xerife*, not *paledrivers* -- way beyond the established pale that's lit by radio frequencies. Where it goes silent."
"It's an old ballad about a young girl who falls in love with a daring boiadeiro. He promises to marry her as soon as he returns from the Western Plain."
"It's diamonds, lawman. Obviously." She grins.
"Just before Gabriel it was the coronation of Franconegro -- now *there* was a real man..." There is no aberration in the pattern that you can see. She puts her foot down.
"Just this month I made half a dozen trips from Saramiriza to Graad, on the U41-A. What do you think they take from Saramiriza to Graad, lawman?"
"Lawman," she greets you. "You caught me at an opportune moment. This awful weather keeps me awake. You can entertain me with your questions."
"Lawman... what in the name of god are you talking about?"
"Like Gabriel Buenguerro in 'O Céu Dourado'..." She nods and smiles, unkindly. "You're the opposite of me then. I remember everything -- even the things I never knew."
"Like Gabriel Buenguerro in 'Pergunte à Poeira.'" She nods and smiles, unkindly. "You're the opposite of me, then. I remember everything -- even things I never knew."
"Like Gabriel Buenguerro in 'Segure-me, Paraíso'..." She nods and smiles, unkindly. "You're the opposite of me then. I remember everything -- even the things I never knew."
"Like looking into the ocean at night. In the dark."
"Lomonossov's Land. Udachnaya Zemlya. The Western Plain..." She nods and closes her eyes again, letting her mind submerge...
"Maybe you've been down the *Motorway South?*" She looks at her cigarette, it's almost out. She has swallowed it hungrily. Then at you...
"Neither is pale transportation." She shrugs. "Life is transitory."
"Never mind," she sighs. "I remember now. I'm still stuck in that traffic jam. In the *Fifties*," she adds with contempt.
"No -- the same one. A *roller*. They all are nowadays. Special wheels for connecting to the floor of the hold." She points to the machines, clumped up like toys.
"No offence, but *your partner*..." She lights the cigarette, a white and silver cloud of smoke disappears into her mouth.
"No one knows what's at the *end...*" She takes the cigarette out of the cigarette holder and extinguishes it. "I've only glimpsed the beginning."
"No, lawman. Diamonds." She grins.
"No, the boiadeiro strangles his beloved and throws her body in the Magritte. Then he rides off, because the Western Plain is calling to him."

"Nothing. Until it starts. When you're deep enough -- then, for me... it's like autumn. Dark grey and orange, the orange of streetlights and the colour of trees in the electric light. It smells like autumn too. It smells terrible."
"Now what do you want with an old woman's boots, *xerife*?"
"Of course it does -- what did you expect?"
"Of course not," she says, grinning. "But wouldn't it be marvellous if I was?"

"Of course not. The boiadeiro returns from the Western Plain a *changed* man. One night, as he and his beloved are out walking along the River Magritte, she pleads with him to give up his riding and settle down..."
"Of course not. To truly understand the boiadeiro, you need to listen to 'On the Western Plain'."
"Of course you don't."
"Oh, don't worry about me. I'm one of the best camionneurs around. I drive routes no one else will."
"Oh, it's so much more than *high* where I go, xerife. It's *low* -- I go to the bottom..." She closes her eyes in reverie.
"Or -- I can just relax and let my mind carry me back where it will. To the great plains..."
"Perhaps it was another *xerife* who came and woke me up, looking at my boots, asking questions? Or perhaps it was one of the others in this *carnaval*. I don't remember."
"Please?" She raises her boot, slowly, with contempt. "I think you should let me get back to Gabriel Buenguerro. You're no Gabriel. Gabriel doesn't say please..."
"So the boiadeiro strangles his beloved and throws her body in the Magritte. Then he rides off, because the Western Plain is calling to him."
"Some jamboree you turned out to be... You have about a third of the jawline of Gabriel Buenguerro, and none of the balls." She smiles.
"Some of them. Some of them are like home to me now." She nods. "I would say the routes I drive are *usual* to me."
"The *most* beautiful -- a true boiadeiro needs a whole horizon to himself. He can't be tied down by man or woman. His beloved was selfish. She didn't know what it meant to love a *boiadeiro*."
"The Trans-Katla Magistral. U41-A. As Estradas do Mirador. All the good ones. The deep trenches. Where the bluebirds fly." She opens her eyes again and shudders.
"The big ones. The tracts. There's no women and men there, it's all just..." She hums along, as if to a track on repeat...
"The feet of a little girl," she smiles. "They fit well on the pedals.
"The feet of a little girl," she smiles. "They fit well on the pedals."

"The look on her face -- like an orgasm. The wound in her chest. My hand in my father's hand..." She closes her eyes, her eyelids trembling. "Except I never had a father. And I never shot Her Innocence Dolores Dei."
"The men have small jaws and everything is made out of plastic. Why do you need plastic?" she scoffs. "When you can make the world out of amber?"

"The smell of liquor on Gabriel's lips after the shoot. In the motor park. The roses on the day of Franconegro's coronation. On the grand stairs of Raehl. The smoke from the fowling piece, when Dolores Dei was shot..."
"Then I don't suppose you could tell me where we are, lawman?"
"Then it's contraband, lawman. What? Do you want to take an old woman in? Be my guest. Lock me away like Bad Hand Hermenegildo."
"Then what *were* you getting at?"
"They are someone's memories, boy." She gets gruff, suddenly. "What difference does it make if it's me or not?"

"They say there is a point -- one that *I* have not crossed -- in the pale superdeep. If you stray too far off course on the U41-A, or in Lomonossov's Land... where every step you take is one step further from home, no matter the direction."
"They're beautiful. That is all that matters. Beautiful and true -- and they will win. They're *coming* for this, you know..." She looks around. "All of this."
"Thought insertion? *Dithering*? The Graad-Katla Magistral?" She savours the lungful. "It's more than dangerous -- it's *sad*. But... at first I had to make a living. Now..."
"Thought insertion? *Dithering*? The Graad-Katla Magistral?" She savours the lungful. "There's a kind of wonder there -- a *sad* wonder. But... at first I had to make a living. Now..."
"Until you came along, that is." The look she gives you is accusatory.
"What are we *doing* here? For thousands of years, Gabriel... It doesn't have to be like this. We can just give up. We can just become vapour."
"What do I need drugs for, lawman? What I see, what I *feel*, the Great Adversary... no drugs can compare."
"What do you mean?"
"When you've seen it all go *away* like that, rolling off like the sea, and then come back to this..." She gestures at the square. The broken horse monument, the clanging of machines in the distance.
"When you've seen it all go *away* like that. Rolling off like the sea. And then come back to this..." She gestures at the square: the broken horse monument, the shadows of the machines in the night.
"Where am I? Who are you?" Like a magician recalling a subject from hypnosis, you've jolted her back to reality.
"Where do you want me to go? This isn't so bad. I can listen to music, or the seagulls. Look at all the colours and the features of this world. It's a good palate-cleanser, this jamboree..."
"While *you* people were tearing each other apart over your petty little Revolution, in Mesque it was a golden age."
"Who the fuck is Evrart?"

"Why not, *xerife*? It's not like I have anything better to do in this hellhole." She settles back against the railing of her motor lorry. Behind her, mountains of memorabilia, photos, and knicknacks line the dashboard.
"Why would I want to do that?"
"Yes -- go. Enough jamboree. I need to get back to Mesque..." Her voice trails off.
"Yes. There is a *protagonista*..." She gestures to the intersection. "And an *adversário*. I am on the side of the Adversary. There's no coming back from that haul."
"Yes. What about it?"
"Yes."
"You *are* an idiot. And you're keeping me here. Glued to this racket. Unless there was anything else..." She puts the cigarette out and stares at something in the distance.
"You cannot see it but you know it's there. And it's big -- bigger than anything. Bigger than all the other things combined."
"You don't need to turn back time. The pale is already churning with it. As the tide of pale rises, so does the past. Someday both will cover the whole world. That's it. That's the story."
"You go right ahead, lawman. Let me know when you find them. I can't wait to read their *report*..."
"You have to understand -- a true boiadeiro needs a whole horizon to himself. He can't be tied down by man or woman. His beloved was selfish. She didn't know what it meant to love a *boiadeiro*."
"You hear that, lawman? I don't think your partner likes you spending too much time with me..."
"Your *mãe*, lawman. What of it?"
